title: Node Classification Beyond Homophily: Towards a General Solution

problem.claim: Existing GNNs commonly rely on homophily, but this assumption can fail and degrade node-classification performance.

gap.claim: Existing approaches for heterophilic graphs are often specific to particular GNN models and therefore lack generality.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes ALT, a family of general structure-learning solutions for node classification across graphs with low or high homophily.
ALT learns to decompose a graph, extract complementary graph signals, and adaptively integrate them for node classification.
Graph signal processing analysis indicates that ALT can give existing GNNs adaptive filter characteristics and modulate input graph signals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant and consistent node-classification performance improvements across a wide range of GNNs and real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely used for graph learning tasks.
Many GNNs assume homophily, which may fail and harm performance.
Heterophily-oriented GNNs exist, but many are tied to specific models and lack generality.
ALT addresses the problem through general structure learning, graph decomposition, signal extraction, and adaptive integration.
The framework is analyzed through graph signal processing and is reported to improve node classification across models and datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the ALT architecture or optimization procedure.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results, dataset names, baselines, or evaluation settings.
The abstract does not describe limitations or failure cases.
